title: Slow-cooker overnight porridge
subtitle: Warm, creamy porridge ready when you wake up
excerpt: Porridge oats and milk slow-cooked overnight in the slow cooker. Wake up to a warm, creamy breakfast with no morning effort required.
sourceNotes: Slow-cooker overnight porridge is a practical method developed by home cooks in the early 2010s. Using oats and liquid on the lowest heat setting overnight produces a very creamy result. The method became widely popular through food blogs.

content.text: This recipe uses the slow cooker's lowest setting overnight. The result is very creamy porridge with a soft, almost custard-like texture that is different from porridge made on the hob. Porridge oats work well; jumbo oats produce a chewier result with more texture.

A thin layer of oats may stick to the base of the pot. Lining with a piece of baking paper or buttering the base before adding the oats helps. Alternatively, use a water bath method: put the oats in a heatproof bowl inside the slow cooker and fill the slow cooker with water halfway up the outside of the bowl.
Serve with honey, a pinch of sea salt, fresh fruit, or a spoonful of jam.

Add {{porridge-oats}} of porridge oats to the slow cooker. Pour over {{whole-milk}} of whole milk and 400ml of cold water. Add {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and stir. Set to LOW, put the lid on, and leave overnight for 7 to 8 hours.
In the morning, stir the porridge well. It will be very thick. Add a splash of hot water or milk to loosen it to your preferred consistency. Serve in bowls with a drizzle of {{honey}} if using.

rows.symptom: The oats have stuck and burned on the base
rows.cause: The slow cooker ran too hot on LOW, or the oat-to-liquid ratio was too low.
rows.fix: Line the base of the slow cooker pot with baking paper before adding the oats. Or use the water bath method: put everything in a heatproof bowl and set inside the slow cooker with water around it.

rows.symptom: The porridge is too thick and stodgy
rows.cause: The oats absorbed all the liquid overnight.
rows.fix: Stir in 100 to 200ml of hot milk to loosen. Add it in stages until you reach the consistency you want.

rows.cause: The slow cooker ran too cool and the oats did not fully gelatinise.
rows.fix: Set to HIGH for 15 minutes and stir every 5 minutes. The porridge will thicken quickly.

rows.cause: Porridge without salt will taste flat.
rows.fix: Add a pinch more salt and stir well. A little extra honey or a pinch of cinnamon will also help.

content.text: Porridge has been a morning staple in Scotland and northern England for centuries. The slow-cooker overnight method is a modern adaptation that removes all morning effort. It suits anyone who wants a warm, filling breakfast without standing at the hob. The method became popular via food blogs in the early 2010s and has stayed because it works.
